extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers preparing an application to the Wellcome Early‑Career Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the Wellcome Early‑Career Awards (Discovery Research). Covers who can apply, how applications are assessed, and what costs can be requested and how to cost them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead applicant career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead applicant career stage: Early‑career researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scheme provides funding for early‑career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and, by the end of the award, be ready to lead their own independent research programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required research training / qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: At the point you submit your application, you must have completed a substantive period of research training relevant to your discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must have: completed a PhD (or equivalent higher research degree) and passed your viva by the application deadline; or, if you have not started a PhD, at least four years' equivalent research experience (e.g., in humanities and social sciences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral experience limit and allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may have some postdoctoral experience, but no more than three years at the point of the application deadline unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted your research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing postdoc experience, Wellcome will allow for part‑time work, the impact of the Covid‑19 pandemic, career breaks (parental leave, long‑term sick leave) and time spent outside research (e.g., clinical training). They will also consider discipline changes and may allow applicants whose three years of postdoc experience fall within a specified transitional window between earlier and later deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research experience evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be able to demonstrate a good understanding of research methodology and evidence of project delivery and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should not need close supervision to complete the proposed research, though you may need retraining in new techniques or approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum time contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should not spend more than 20% of your time on non‑research activities (clinical duties, teaching, administration). If you're in a clinical craft specialty, you may spend up to 40% on clinical duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health professional registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a health professional and want to continue clinical activities, you must be registered with and licensed by the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Q&As for health professionals for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organisation location and type
rubrics_metrics.description: The administering organisation must be in the UK, Republic of Ireland, or a low‑ or middle‑income country (apart from India and mainland China) and be not‑for‑profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible organisation types include higher education institutions, research institutes and healthcare organisations. The administering organisation is responsible for submitting the final application and managing finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational grant conditions and core funding restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Your grant must be administered by an eligible organisation that can sign up to Wellcome grant conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the administering organisation is core‑funded, an Early‑Career Award should not replace or lead to a reduction in existing or planned core support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research remit fit to Discovery Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery Research supports any discipline (STEM, experimental medicine, humanities, social sciences, clinical/allied health sciences, public health). Research that falls outside Discovery Research remit or that would start earlier than seven months after the application deadline is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a research environment that provides appropriate training, resources and experience to deliver your project and develop research skills and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome encourages moving away from your current research environment (e.g., different group/department) but does not require changing organisations. The environment must support your development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or honorary appointment) for the award duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor responsibilities: guarantee space and resources for the award, ensure the research environment supports project completion, confirm workload expectations (adherence to 80% research time rule). If you plan to work away from the administering organisation for >3 months, an additional sponsor at that location is required. Sponsors are not paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor role and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: You should identify a mentor for the award period with a track record in training and mentorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor should support/manage application preparation, career development, personal development and navigating host organisation processes. Mentor need not be based at the administering organisation; sponsors can also act as mentors. Mentors are not paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborator role and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators support delivery but do not lead specific research components and do not have to meet eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborators cannot receive salary/compensation for time on the project, but you can request costs to cover their expenses (travel, materials) directly related to the research. Collaborators can provide access to facilities, datasets, subject expertise, or organisations led by lived‑experience experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on holding other Wellcome awards
rubrics_metrics.description: During an Early‑Career Award you cannot be the sole applicant on any other Wellcome awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can be a coapplicant on one other Wellcome award if you justify how you'll manage commitments. You can only hold one Early‑Career Award at a time and renewals are not offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsuccessful, you can submit one more application for the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant changes are needed for the second application. You do not need to contact Wellcome before resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: tenured salaried post
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not eligible if you have an existing tenured (salaried) post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low‑ or middle‑income country).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may relinquish an existing tenured post to take up an Early‑Career Award only if your current post is not research‑based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short‑term funding allowance prior to application
rubrics_metrics.description: Short‑term funding from administering organisation or learned societies that supported transition from doctoral to postdoctoral research is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: funding for developing new research ideas, career progression, networking, travel or residencies after PhD. Combined duration of short‑term funding cannot exceed three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment weighting overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be reviewed on: research proposal (50%), your skills and experience (25%), and your research environment (25%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment weightings are used at interview stage. Wellcome also offers opportunities to observe advisory committees to learn how applications are assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal — Bold
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive proposals should be 'Bold' — aim to deliver a significant shift in understanding and/or provide a significant advance over existing methodologies, conceptual frameworks, tools or techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal should have the potential to stimulate new and innovative research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal — Creative
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed approach should be 'Creative' — novel concepts, methods or technologies, or novel combinations of existing ideas and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should develop and test new concepts, methods or technologies, or combine existing approaches in new ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal — High quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be high quality: well‑designed, clear, supported by evidence and have feasible proposed outcomes/outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility and clarity are emphasised; provide supporting evidence and realistic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills and experience — evaluation points
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess your previous research outputs and contributions, research skills and experience of different methodologies, and plans to develop management skills for leading a research programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate track record, methodological breadth, and a plan for leadership and management development during the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment — evaluation points
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess how your research environment(s) will support delivery of the research programme and your development as a researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the administering organisation will develop your project and management skills and how you will contribute to a positive and inclusive research culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and duration constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Award provides a salary for the grantholder and up to £400,000 for research expenses; usually lasts 5 years but may be shorter for some disciplines; may be longer only if held part‑time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost the application at 1.0 FTE when applying; Wellcome will extend duration to reflect part‑time requests. Ask for level and duration of funding justifiable for proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will fund the total cost of your salary for the grant period; you can only receive one salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary should be based on host organisation pay scales and include basic salary, employer’s contributions (statutory obligations, pension), incremental progression and locally recognised allowances. Do not include potential promotion costs or prior Wellcome fellowship supplements. For host organisations in LMIC when working in HIC for ≥12 months, pay at the appropriate rate for that country. Year‑1 pay awards allowed; if unknown use IMF inflation indicator; Year‑2 onwards Wellcome applies inflation allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa and work permit costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If Wellcome is paying your salary on the grant, you can ask for visa and work permit costs to help take up the post at the host organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can include visa costs for partner/dependants, Immigration Health Surcharge for UK stays ≥6 months, and essential associated costs (travel to visa appointments, English tests) if justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff costs limit and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will provide salary costs for staff who work on your project up to the equivalent of a 36‑month full‑time post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 24 months for a research assistant + 12 months for a technician. You can ask for more for specialist service staff/technical experts or support related to disability/long‑term health conditions. Wellcome does not provide studentships on this award.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cost salaries for research staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff salaries should be appropriate to skills/responsibilities. Host organisation should use their salary scales to calculate costs including basic salary, employer contributions, Apprentice Levy (UK), incremental progression and local allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for salary pay awards in Year‑1 (use IMF inflation indicator if unknown). From Year‑2 use organisation’s current pay rates; Wellcome provides a separate salary inflation allowance. Read grantholder and host responsibilities guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability‑related adjustment support
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment support can be requested if you or a staff member is disabled or has a long‑term health condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs can include additional staff for day‑to‑day project activities, assistive technology, and care costs for assistance animals when travelling. Wellcome will not pay for capital/building costs (e.g., access ramps). They will only cover what government/employer does not and may be asked for after award if costs are unknown at application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have to move to take up the post you can ask for up to £1,000 for personal removal costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must explain why you need this in your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing professional development and training costs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can request costs for professional skills training and research skills training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the administering organisation does not provide adequate training, you can ask for up to £500 a year for you and each member of staff on the grant (subject to role and FTE thresholds). Research skills training costs require justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and consumables coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay for materials and consumables needed to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes laboratory chemicals/materials, project‑specific PPE above standard, printing for fieldwork/empirical research, shipping/delivery/freight charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals — costs and conditions (full economic costing orgs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organisation uses full economic costing methodology you can ask to buy animals if essential, and Wellcome will fund animal house charge‑out rates and associated running costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs include running costs, licences, relevant staff training, appropriate estates costs and cage/equipment depreciation (not building depreciation). For UK research using macaques, they must be sourced from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Wellcome may not pay full charge‑out rates if it has significantly funded the facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals — costs and conditions (non‑full economic costing orgs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your organisation does not use full economic costing you can ask for costs to cover buying/transporting animals and running costs, staff contributions, equipment maintenance, microbiological monitoring, waste disposal, licences, training and enrichment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will not provide estates costs or cage/building depreciation in these cases. Macaque purchases from the Centre for Macaques are not counted against the £400,000 research expenses limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment purchase and maintenance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for equipment purchase where it is not available at your administering organisation or via collaborations and you will be the main user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 50% of use must be for Wellcome‑funded activities. Costs can include purchase, delivery, installation, maintenance and training. Second‑hand equipment is allowed if more environmentally sustainable. VAT/import duties covered in certain circumstances. Maintenance covered for equipment funded by Wellcome or another source when essential, five years old (or will become five), cost‑effective and environmentally sustainable to maintain; not covered where access charges can recoup costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer equipment and software rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will cover one personal computer/laptop per person working on the grant and software/software licences and recurring computing costs linked to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs should be reasonable and justified. ERN/ELN software covered on a per user, per year basis for the duration. Wellcome will not pay for significantly expensive items without justification, installation/training costs, or access charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access charges to shared equipment/facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for cost of access to shared equipment, facilities or services if essential to your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include materials/consumables and a proportion of maintenance/service contracts and staff time for dedicated technical staff. Wellcome does not cover estates/utilities/depreciation/insurance or other departmental staff time except where related to animal housing facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overheads policy and evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for overheads if your grant will be based at an eligible organisation (HEI, healthcare, research institute outside UK or UK org that does not receive core funding for overheads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overheads are not counted against the £400,000 research expenses limit and should not be more than 20% of direct research costs. Applicants must provide a letter from their Finance Director confirming how overheads have been calculated; if validated methodology exists, include confirmation of validated rate, how it was arrived at, last review and where details can be found. If not validated, provide a breakdown and confirmation it represents true costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmentally conscious travel policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel on grants should be done in an environmentally conscious way, in line with Wellcome's environmental sustainability funding policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider replacing travel with videoconferencing or virtual attendance. Where travel is necessary, ask for low‑carbon modes even if more expensive (e.g., train instead of flying). Economy flights allowed when train journeys >10 hours or where safety/visa/availability/exceptional circumstances apply. Wellcome will not pay business class. You may request carbon credits to mitigate essential travel emissions, or equivalent sustainability initiatives, with organisational approval prior to application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference attendance cost limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits for conference attendance costs: Grantholder £2,000 a year; research/technical staff on grant £1,000 each a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may also ask for accredited carbon credits to mitigate conference travel emissions in addition to these limits. Caring responsibilities costs for conference attendance can be requested (up to £1,000 per person per conference) under specific conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel — outward/return travel rules and partners/dependants
rubrics_metrics.description: Where travel is necessary, people are expected to travel by train for end‑to‑end journeys of 10 hours or less; flights covered only in specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will not pay business class. They may provide travel costs for partners/dependants when overseas for more than 12 months and may provide for shorter trips if justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodation and subsistence rules by duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Different rules apply depending on length of stay: up to one month subsistence (accommodation, meals, incidentals); 1–12 months reasonable rental costs only; more than 12 months housing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employing organisation has subsistence policy use that; otherwise use HMRC rates. If from LMIC and working in HIC for >1 month up to 12 months, you can ask for up to £10/day extra to cover extra costs. Discuss appropriate rental rates with organisations/Wellcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baggage and freight shipping allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowances for baggage/freight differ by duration: up to 12 months you can ask for up to 80kg additional baggage or unaccompanied freight; more than 12 months you can ask for shipping personal items (half container if alone, whole container if with partner/dependants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome will pay these costs as part of relocation/overseas allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical, travel insurance and emergency evacuation
rubrics_metrics.description: If travelling outside home country Wellcome will pay medical and travel insurance costs where appropriate and emergency evacuation cover for work in LMICs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do not pay medical insurance for trips to UK/ROI. For UK trips up to six months take travel insurance; for >6 months Wellcome will cover the Immigration Health Surcharge instead of medical insurance. Wellcome will cover emergency evacuation cover if working in LMICs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visas and vaccinations coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay costs of visas, vaccinations and anti‑malaria treatment, including costs required for immigration applications (e.g., Immigration Health Surcharge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are already in the country you will be working in, visa costs may be taxable; Wellcome will cover tax related to these costs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing security costs for overseas placements
rubrics_metrics.description: If based in an LMIC for >1 month and necessary, you can ask for housing security costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs can include guards, panic buttons and alarms; consult employing organisation for advice on appropriate security level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas allowances for long stays (>12 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you or staff will spend more than 12 months in another country, Wellcome provides overseas allowances in addition to standard travel/subsistence and these are not counted against the £400,000 research expenses limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowances include contributions to personal costs to avoid disadvantage, provided on assumption you will pay income tax in home or host country and that you/partner will not receive equivalent allowances elsewhere. Includes partners/dependants, accommodation (based on market data or consultation), education allowances with caps and exclusions, annual leave travel schedule, and language lessons (truncated in page but covered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education allowances for children during overseas placements
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for local nursery/school fees or local international school fees where local education isn't equivalent; boarding school fees in home country considered in specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local nursery/school fees up to maximum of 30 hours/week for 3–4 year olds; for international schools Wellcome will pay published termly school fees only. They will not cover extracurriculars, uniforms, transport, books, electronic equipment. Boarding school fees: may cover published termly fees up to £30,000/year per child and return travel/emission mitigation at term start/end in line with sustainability policy, in specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual leave travel entitlements for long overseas stays
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay an annual leave return trip to home country based on duration of overseas appointment (e.g., 12–24 months = 1 trip; 25–36 months = 2 trips; and so on).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fares should align with environmental sustainability policy and be booked in advance where possible. Business class not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of justification and costing best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must justify costs requested and, where applicable, provide organisational evidence (e.g., Finance Director letter for overheads) and explain why certain costs are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome expects applicants to cost appropriately for the local context, may request costs in a currency that fits where research will be conducted (explain exchange rate used), and will contact applicants if queries arise.
